page: Microsoft Azure D48as_v4 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the DASv4 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 48 virtual CPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. It is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced allocation of 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Local storage consists of a 393 GB solid-state drive, and the instance is capable of utilizing Premium Storage.

In benchmark evaluations, the D48as_v4 demonstrates strong multi-core and single-core CPU performance, placing in the top 25% for stress-ng tests. Its memory subsystem is highly efficient, achieving a top-tier rating in the PassMark memory score. Cryptographic capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated AES, VAES, and SHA-NI instruction sets, resulting in strong performance in encryption benchmarks. Multi-threaded decompression and image processing also rank in the top 25%. However, large-scale language model inference shows limitations, with text generation for 70B models falling into the bottom 25% of tested systems.

This virtual machine is managed via the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor and provides dedicated CPU allocation. Given its balanced resource distribution and strong multi-threaded processing capabilities, the server is well-suited for workloads such as multi-threaded decompression, image processing, and general-purpose enterprise applications. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the D48as_v4 offers a dense allocation of physical cores and high-tier memory performance within a standard general-purpose hardware profile, making it a viable option for resource-intensive tasks that do not require dedicated GPU acceleration.
